risks: Non-deterministic tie-break in -releaseDate sort makes page/offset-based pagination unreliable across separate runs; must dedup by stable game id, not by offset/page number.

No verified working method to fetch a third-party YouTube video's transcript from a typical cloud server IP: official API cannot do it at all (OAuth+owner-only), unofficial scraping returned an empty body in a live test from this environment and is documented to be blocked by ASN on AWS/GCP/Azure/Hetzner/DigitalOcean.
YouTube Data API v3 default quota (100 search.list calls/day) is incompatible at face value with processing 20 games/hour if 1 search is issued per game.
backend.metacritic.com is an undocumented private API with no published rate limit or SLA; behavior under sustained production load was not tested.

www.metacritic.com blocks specific literal User-Agent strings (python-requests, Java/) via Cloudflare WAF; trivially fixed today but could be tightened without notice, unlike backend.metacritic.com which showed no such blocking in any test performed.
stats endpoint reviewCount (all ratings) can exceed reviews-list totalResults (text-only reviews) — summarization pipelines must not assume these numbers match.
Site is Nuxt 3, not Next.js as assumed in the task; __NEXT_DATA__ does not exist, only __NUXT_DATA__ in the devalue flattened-array format.
top_5_facts_for_architecture: An open, unauthenticated, non-rate-limited-in-testing JSON API exists at backend.metacritic.com and should be the primary data source instead of HTML/Nuxt scraping.
Metascore per platform comes for free with the single product call; Userscore per platform requires one additional call per platform — external call count scales with number of platforms per game.

The official YouTube API can never return a third party's caption text (OAuth+owner-only restriction); the only path to a transcript is unofficial scraping/yt-dlp, which is documented and empirically observed here to be unreliable specifically on cloud/datacenter IPs — this feature should be designed as best-effort/degradable, not guaranteed.
New-releases pagination is not idempotent across separate hourly runs (no stable sort tie-break) — dedup must key off game id, not offset/page number.

Ready-made sentiment-bucketed review 'summary' endpoints (default/positive/negative/neutral quotes) exist and could reduce the review-summarization pipeline's need to paginate and bucket the full review list manually.
